546: The vulnerability allowed for the changing of email addresses without verification, potentially enabling unauthorized access to user accounts.
575: Email spoofing was identified as a security vulnerability, allowing attackers to send emails that appear to be from a different sender. This could potentially lead to reputation loss and fraudulent activities.
46397: An insecure direct object reference vulnerability was discovered in the program portal. By manipulating the user ID in the delete request URL, it was possible to generate delete notifications for users who were not invited as participants in a bug report. This could lead to unauthorized removal notifications being sent to users and confusion among admins and participants.
46916: A markdown parsing issue was discovered that enabled insertion of malicious tags and event handlers. When markdown was presented as HTML, an interaction between `_` and `@` allowed an attacker to insert tags with arbitrary attributes like event handlers. This could lead to cross-site scripting if event handlers were allowed to execute.
48422: Invitations to sandboxed teams in HackerOne were not consistently invalidated when accepted, allowing users to reuse the invitation link and join the team multiple times.
49566: An auto-approval vulnerability allowed invited HackerOne users to become team members without their knowledge or consent if they clicked on the invitation link while not logged into their HackerOne account. The option to accept or reject the invitation was not displayed, resulting in automatic acceptance.
63729: A logic error in the notification system allowed a user who had left a team to continue receiving notifications about updates to bugs associated with that team. The user was unable to remove themselves from the notification list, even after leaving the team.
75556: The title of a bug report, for which a user was marked as a duplicate, was leaked on the Reputation log page, potentially exposing sensitive information.
83604: An HTML injection vulnerability was discovered in the "linkSuccess=" parameter of the Khan Academy website which could allow arbitrary HTML code to be executed.
90308: A vulnerability was discovered that allowed user email addresses to be enumerated on the Coinbase platform. Through scripting, large lists of possible email addresses could be generated and imported as contacts into a Coinbase account. The feature that notified users inviting contacts which emails belonged to existing Coinbase members revealed emails that were in use, compromising privacy. As a result, the notification mechanism was modified to no longer disclose account information to inviters while still sending invites as intended.
90862: Passwords submitted in a signup form were returned in clear text in later responses from the application, increasing the risk of password capture.
97191: A same-origin policy violation vulnerability was discovered that allowed an attacker to send AJAX requests from a specific domain to an external domain. This vulnerability could potentially lead to cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.
103989: A vulnerability was exploited where throwing a malformed error from within an iframe caused user-provided data to be interpreted as HTML by an error handling component. This allowed arbitrary JavaScript code to be executed. The issue was addressed by sanitizing all messages passed from iframes prior to use.
